# Production classes no mount point reaches.
#
# GENERATED — do not edit the class list. Re-record with:
#     ./gradlew :core:harness:reachLedger
#
# The REASON is yours and regeneration keeps it. A new entry arrives
# as REASON MISSING and the build fails until somebody says which of
# these it is:
#
#   an external consumer   — name them; this store's API is used
#                            outside this repository
#   reached by a mechanism the ledger cannot see — say which, and
#                            prefer teaching the ledger over writing
#                            this down
#   NOT REACHED            — the defect this file exists to surface:
#                            built, proven, and mounted by nothing
#
# Activators, SPI providers, karaf commands and main classes are
# reachable and are not listed: they are found from the manifest,
# from META-INF/services, from their annotations and from their own
# signature.
cloud.jengu.dbo.asking.Across                                            an external consumer: the binding a product holds when it is across a network from the tenant, which is why nothing here builds one. The other binding is registered on the whiteboard because a tenant has a store to hand it; this one needs a URL and a token that belong to somebody else's process, and a deployment constructing one would be this repository pretending to be its own consumer
cloud.jengu.dbo.auth.SecretHashProbe                                     a test's way into a package-private verifier — SecretHash itself is reached, and widening it to test it is the worse trade
cloud.jengu.dbo.fhir.common.ArchiveProvenance                            NOT REACHED — the FHIR rendering of an archive's attestation, and no export path builds one
cloud.jengu.dbo.fhir.element.DefinitionEnvelopeProbe                     a test's way to a package-private builder, as SecretHashProbe is. The envelope can be built from expressions the face writes out or from the parameters the cut compiled, and holding the two to the same answer needs a tenant, so the test lives in the harness and cannot see the class. Making the builder public to test it would put two front ends and their whole vocabulary on the exported surface, where the api ledger would then hold us to them
cloud.jengu.dbo.fhir.index.BoundCodes                                    NOT REACHED — the codes a required binding is decided against, beside the index. 520 of them for a face root's closure, which is the measurement that said this is not an expansion problem. Only a checker asks it, and nothing asks the checker. DefinitionIndex and DefinitionRows left this file when the face's envelope builder began naming them, and that is this ledger's own class-level limit rather than a serving path: the builder is reached, the front end that reads compiled parameters is not called by any mount yet, and a dead method on a live class is invisible here. Said where somebody reading a shorter file would otherwise conclude the index is mounted
cloud.jengu.dbo.fhir.r4.R4Subscriptions                                  NOT REACHED — and wholly superseded: both halves, criteria and topic, are composed on the element face now, which is what serves tenants. This hangs off R4Store, which no request reaches. Deleting it is filed; the R4 backport inside it is the only answer written to where an R4 topic lives, so that goes first
cloud.jengu.dbo.fhir.r5.R5Subscriptions                                  NOT REACHED — and wholly superseded: both halves, criteria and topic, are composed on the element face now, which is what serves tenants. This hangs off R5Store, which no request reaches. Deleting it is filed, and waits only on its R4 twin
cloud.jengu.dbo.fhir.validate.ElementChecks                              NOT REACHED — the checks over the index: cardinality, fixed, pattern, slicing, required bindings and the compiled rules. Every one is held against the database's own answer over everything the version publishes and agrees. Agreeing is not being asked, and no write asks it
cloud.jengu.dbo.fhir.validate.IndexPayloads                              NOT REACHED — deliberately, and it is now the whole chain's root. It implements the payload contract over the index rather than a worker context, and meets all five parts of it: read, type, write back, check, shape stamp. Nothing selects it for a tenant, so no write asks it anything and no megabyte has moved. THIRD TIME THIS FILE HAS SHRUNK WITHOUT ANYTHING CHANGING: DefinitionRows left when Envelope named it, ElementChecks left when this named it, and the ledger asks whether a production class names another rather than whether anything reaches the root. Four entries have become one. What takes it out is a tenant that declares this face
cloud.jengu.dbo.maintenance.ReferenceClosure                             NOT REACHED — not on a maintenance route, not a console command, not in the verifier
cloud.jengu.dbo.promises.Proving                                         the annotation a test cites a promise with — read by the projection, never by the runtime
cloud.jengu.dbo.runner.ProvingLane                                       an external consumer — implementors prove their own step services with it, which is the whole of what it is for. The driver-probe bundle names it too and deliberately does not count: a probe is not production reach, and a ledger a probe could satisfy is one anybody could satisfy by writing one
cloud.jengu.dbo.sync.http.HttpLanes                                      an external consumer: a host that drives a tenant's replication over HTTP from its own process, which is why it is not built in this one
cloud.jengu.dbo.tenant.k8s.SpecDirSync                                   NOT REACHED — the spec mount for a process with no ConfigMap volume, and the operator builds none
cloud.jengu.dbo.work.Runner                                              an external consumer: the embeddable participant, built by whatever process does the work — a hospital's integration, an edge with no orchestrator
cloud.jengu.dbo.work.WorkScopedStore                                     NOT REACHED — and the replication lane reads the manifest it would write, so a travelling run carries none of what it made
